The files in this folder are data of GeoSphere Austria, from its Data Hub,
https://data.hub.geosphere.at, dataset "nowcast-v1-15min-1km"
(Kurzfristwettervorhersagen für Österreich, DOI 10.60669/ahad-4y43). The
dataset's page, https://data.hub.geosphere.at/dataset/nowcast-v1-15min-1km,
read on 2026-11-21, names its licence: "Creative Commons Namensnennung 4.0
International". The Data Hub's legal page, https://data.hub.geosphere.at/legal
(the German text is the binding one), read on the same day, says: "Soweit
der/die Datenempfänger:in die von der GeoSphere Austria erstellten Daten
verwendet, hat er/sie die GeoSphere Austria als Urheberin und
Rechteinhaberin in folgender Weise nennen: „Datenquelle: GeoSphere Austria -
https://data.hub.geosphere.at“." They are not covered by the licence of
the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-21 from
https://dataset.api.hub.geosphere.at/v1/grid/forecast/nowcast-v1-15min-1km,
without an account or a key, with curl and the user agent the server's
fetcher sends ("venti-server/0.1.0"). Each is the whole answer to one
request of the adapter, unchanged:

    metadata.json   GET .../nowcast-v1-15min-1km/metadata
                    asked at 13:17:11 UTC, answered some 15 seconds
                    later, 1,588 bytes: the dataset's description and the
                    six runs the service holds, by their reference times,
                    11:45 to 13:00 UTC

    rr-202611211245.nc   425,558 bytes
                    GET ...?parameters=rr&bbox=46.25,9.35,48.55,17.25
                        &forecast_offset=1
                        &start=2026-11-21T12:45&end=2026-11-21T12:45
                        &output_format=netcdf
                    asked at 13:17:35 UTC, answered within a second

    rr-202611211300.nc   426,204 bytes
                    GET ...?parameters=rr&bbox=46.25,9.35,48.55,17.25
                        &forecast_offset=0
                        &start=2026-11-21T13:00&end=2026-11-21T13:00
                        &output_format=netcdf
                    asked at 13:17:36 UTC, answered some 44 seconds later

The box is the first region's, 46.3,9.4,48.5,17.2, widened by a twentieth
of a degree on every side, as the adapter asks for it. They were recorded
in the same two minutes as DWD's radar frames in
crates/sources-dwd-radar/tests/fixtures, so that one clock is honest for
both: the server's development mode shows the two as layers of one moment,
by a radar clock at 13:19 UTC. They replace a recording of 12:39 UTC on
the same day (the runs of 12:00 and 12:15, 407,953 and 407,258 bytes),
which was asked for with the plain box: its rectangle of 600 by 252 points
left 107 cells in the middle of the last row of the region's map without a
value.

Each of the two is the first step of one run of INCA's nowcast, the step at
the run's own reference time: the precipitation sum "rr" in kg m-2 of the
quarter of an hour that ends then, for the part of the model's grid of one
kilometre (EPSG:31287, MGI / Austria Lambert) that the widened box of the
first region asks for: 608 by 263 points, 159,904 values (the answer's
header datapoint-count). Every one of the 162,864 cells of the region's
map lies within it and has a value. The files are netCDF-4, which is HDF5. The box is asked
for and not the whole domain because the service lets a request name one;
the whole domain is 701 by 431 points.

Not kept here, asked on the same day to learn how the service behaves:
the list of all datasets, the metadata of inca-v1-1h-1km and
inca-v2-1h-1km, the Data Hub's catalogue entries, four requests for a
handful of points as GeoJSON, the list of runs twice more, one first try
at the NetCDF answer, and the three answers of the earlier recording.
Seventeen requests to the dataset service in all on that day, the three
kept here among them; after the last of these its own counter showed 10
used of the 240 an hour it allows.

sha256:
    43322af6f03635a36fda53fdb2a19f6f59b87e5ef96077879f2ac898dc14361a  metadata.json
    cd90098693b584b7ea923ec5123e08cd92f02b21801c57788a090067af7df60f  rr-202611211245.nc
    212f2f05b2b5f0e08487d4421d8038939c32bdd7dcaf0414205709780292cbcb  rr-202611211300.nc

To record them again: ask for the list, then for the first step of the two
runs it names first, each by its place in the list and with the widened
box, and record the other radar source in the same minutes; replace the
three files; set the moments in src/fixtures.rs and the names there; run
the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what changed. The tests
pin what is of that moment (the counts of cells in each step, the size of
the rectangle, where `leadtime` and `x` stand in the older file), and
those will differ.

A frame is an analysis: rain as a model put it together from radars and
gauges. It is no statement that a place is dry, or that it can be flown.
